title: Immune Complex Deposition Patterns in Glomerulonephritis
subject: Pathology
preview: Immune-complex glomerulonephritis commonly produces granular immunofluorescence patterns in glomeruli.
quickRevision: Immune-complex glomerulonephritis commonly produces granular immunofluorescence patterns in glomeruli.
Electron microscopy helps localize deposits as subepithelial, subendothelial or mesangial.
Clinical syndrome, complement testing and serology must be interpreted with biopsy context.

sections.title: Pathophysiology & identification
points: Immune-complex glomerulonephritis commonly produces granular immunofluorescence patterns in glomeruli.
Anti-GBM disease classically produces linear IgG staining along the glomerular basement membrane.

sections.title: Diagnostic and treatment connections
points: Electron microscopy helps localize deposits as subepithelial, subendothelial or mesangial.
Clinical syndrome, complement testing and serology must be interpreted with biopsy context.

sections.title: Exam trap — avoid this mistake
points: A granular pattern is not equivalent to a specific etiologic diagnosis without other evidence.

quiz.question: What immunofluorescence pattern is typical of anti-GBM disease?
quiz.explanation: Linear IgG along basement membranes. Anti-GBM disease classically produces linear IgG staining along the glomerular basement membrane.
